p1_finding.what: js_number uses format!("{:e}", value.abs()) for the shortest round-trip digits and then rearranges the exponent per the ES rules. Rust and ECMAScript both emit a shortest round-trip representation but break ties between equally short candidates differently, so the digits can differ and the sha256 revision over the canonical JSON differs with them.
p1_finding.overclaim_location: the doc comment at src/js.rs:85 and the crate claim at src/lib.rs:12
p1_finding.reproduction: an extra observation field of 1000000000000000.25 inside a snapshot the default profile accepts: both sides project 5000 basis points, JS sourceRevision sha256:db57444e..., Rust sha256:77cabf57...

independently_verified_by_measurement.js: node: String(1000000000000000.25) and JSON.stringify both give 1000000000000000.2
independently_verified_by_measurement.mechanism: the exact value is the midpoint between the two shortest 17-digit candidates. ECMAScript Number::toString breaks that tie to the even last digit; Rust's shortest-representation algorithm does not, so this is a systematic class rather than one input.
independently_verified_by_measurement.conclusion: confirmed. The finding stands as written.

correction_1.wrong_claim: This record said of the in-orchestration review: it ran 12 targeted mutations against the parity harness, which failed under each -- 'that is the check that distinguishes a parity proof from a parity claim.'
correction_1.error_class: a sufficiency claim drawn from a necessary-condition test, and an absence claim with no completeness basis over the input domain. Mutation resistance shows the harness detects changes to the implementation; it says nothing about inputs the corpus does not contain, and EXT-005 shows the same harness also passes an emptied fixture whose header counts were zeroed.
correction_1.downstream_consequence: this record presented byte-level parity as established when it holds only over the corpus. A reader deciding to wire the crate for hash interchange with the JS would have been misled by my wording, not only by the crate's.
correction_1.check_that_would_have_caught_it: a differential probe on number formatting outside the corpus -- the external reviewer's -- or simply asking what the evidence domain is and what lies outside it. The corpus was the whole evidence base and I did not ask that question of it.
correction_1.what_stands: the mutation result itself, and the 32 passing tests, are as recorded. The parity claim is restated as corpus-only.
